propositions: Jira Data Center rate limiting (enabled per-admin, token bucket model introduced in 8.6) returns 429 responses that rebar transport treats as hard failures instead of honourable retry signals.

The existing retry infrastructure in _with_connection_retry explicitly excludes JIRAError (all 4xx/5xx responses) from retry scope to prevent duplicate mutations, creating a structural barrier to adding 429 handling at that choke point.

A 429 can arrive after the server has begun processing a write request, making it indistinguishable from pre-write rejection; retrying mutations on 429 would reintroduce duplicate-issue failures that a prior fix eliminated.

The solution requires extracting retry/error handling code from transport.py (currently at 789/800 line capacity limit) into a separate module, then adding 429 retry support scoped only to idempotent reads via per-call opt-in defaulting to OFF.

Multiple independent reads (direct _with_connection_retry calls in get_comment_map, _paged_search through _call_logged, probe_remote) require the retry flag to propagate through different call chains to be reachable.

The implementation must parse Retry-After headers, apply jitter-then-clamp logic per Atlassian guidance, and ensure exhausted retry attempts surface as BackendHTTPError(code=429) rather than leaking vendor JIRAError types past the adapter boundary.
